choice: A card with the current issue, its parent, a sub-issue progress bar and its open sub-issues; below it the project's board: started and unstarted states, then a collapsed 'Closed · 24h' group (completedAt or canceledAt within -P1D), then a collapsed 'Backlog' group: the project's 100 newest issues in backlog-type states (orderBy: createdAt), newest first, fetched in the same GraphQL request as the board. With more, the count gets a '+' and the group ends with a 'More' link to <project url>/issues. Groups follow workflow state type and name, so the same state of several teams is one group; the backlog is one group whatever its states are called. The current issue and its open sub-issues are left off the board and the backlog. The project header's count leaves the backlog out.
context: Four mockups were compared: a by-status board, a tree around the current issue, a project found by repository link on main, and the empty state. The user defined current issues as In Progress, In Review and Todo plus issues closed in the last 24 hours. Later the user asked for the project's backlog after the closed group; a project can have hundreds of backlog issues, and the user chose to show at most the 100 most recently created, with the rest behind a 'More' link to Linear.
rejected: Board only: no sub-issue context. Tree only: loses the familiar board. Filtering by state names (custom per team) instead of state types. A workspace list inside the panel (not needed once the panel moved to the right sidebar). The whole backlog with pagination (1,000 rows took about half a second per render, and the page re-renders on every change). A separate backlog request with a longer cache and changes merged in (an extra request and a backlog out of step with the board, for a list capped at 100). Linking 'More' to /team/<KEY>/backlog (the team's backlog across all its projects).
title: Panel layout: current-issue card with sub-issues above the project's status board and its newest backlog
